title: The Radio Continuum Source Projected Near HR 8799
question: Is the radio continuum source seen near HR 8799 (VLA 3 GHz and ALMA 340 GHz) physically associated with the star/exoplanets, or is it a background galaxy?

what.value: 3 GHz source counts and spectral index distribution

evidence.quote: we have used the 3.0 GHz source catalog of Smolčić et al. (2017) to produce a plot of the expected number of background sources
From the results of Zavala et al. (2017) we estimate that the number of background sources with a flux density of 0.49 mJy or higher at 850 $\mu$m is about 4.9 per square arcmin.
an interpolation of the orbital motions of the exoplanets with respect to the star taken from Konopacky et al. (2016)

what.value: ALMA+ACA fluxes at 340 and 230 GHz and disk inner radius

evidence.loc: 3.3 Comparison between the VLA and the ALMA data
evidence.quote: the data points of Faramaz et al. (2021) have flux densities of 316$\pm$20 and 58$\pm$18 $\mu$Jy, at 340 and 230 GHz, respectively.

recipe.method: Calibrate and concatenate VLA epochs; clean ALMA and VLA images; fit source in image plane with IMFIT
Use background source counts times the solid angle of a 2.2" radius circle
Split the 2-4 GHz band into two 1 GHz halves; compare positions and fluxes in VLA and ALMA and per-epoch
Compare VLA and ALMA positions 5.5 yr apart against expected stellar proper-motion displacement

evidence.quote: the *a priori probability is 0.0046, or 1 in 215.
